oneLiner: 先按需求把市场切成几块，挑最值得服务的一块，再在用户心里给它钉一个清晰位置。
oneLinerEn: Cut the market by need, choose the slice worth serving, then pin a clear place for it in the mind.
detail: STP 是现代营销的战略主线，分三步：市场细分按地理、人口、行为与心理，把参差多样的需求切成一块块内部相近的小市场——真正管用的常是按想要的利益与使用行为来分，而非只按年龄收入分；目标市场选择在细分市场的吸引力与企业自身能力之间权衡，据此选无差异（赌大众）、差异化（多块多版本）或集中化（专注一块）；定位则在你选定的那块用户心智里，为品牌争一个简单、独特、守得住的位置。它是定位理论的上位流程：定位是最后一环，前面若没有正确的细分与取舍，定位再漂亮也悬在半空。STP 逼企业承认不可能服务所有人——敢于放弃，是营销走向成熟的第一标志。
detailEn: STP is the strategic spine of modern marketing, in three moves. Segmentation slices a diverse demand into homogeneous pockets by geography, demographics, behaviour and psychographics — what usually works keys on sought benefits and usage, not age and income alone. Targeting weighs each segment's attractiveness against the firm's own capability, then bets undifferentiated (the whole market), differentiated (many segments, many offers) or concentrated (one niche). Positioning then wins a simple, distinct, defensible place in that chosen slice of the user's mind. It is the higher-level process around the positioning theory: positioning is the last move, and without the right segmentation and trade-offs before it, even a beautiful position floats in mid-air. STP forces a firm to admit it cannot serve everyone — daring to give up is the first sign of marketing maturity.

oneLiner: 产品、价格、渠道、推广四只手要一起调——营销不只是打广告，而是让这四者彼此咬合。
oneLinerEn: Product, price, place and promotion must be tuned together — marketing is not just advertising but meshing all four.
detail: 杰罗姆·麦卡锡把营销的可控手段归成四个 P：产品（解决什么需求、什么功能与品质）、价格（值多少、怎么收费与折让）、渠道（在哪里、如何触达与交付）与推广（广告、公关、促销与人员推销如何让顾客知晓并心动）。它的精髓不是清单，而是一致性：四者必须指向同一类顾客、同一个定位，任何一环拧着来都会漏水——高端定位配地摊渠道，再响的广告也救不回。服务营销又把 7P 补上人员、流程与有形展示。常见误区是把 4P 当成由内而外的自我表达，现代营销更强调它的镜子——4C（顾客需求、成本、便利、沟通）：先问顾客要什么，再决定这四个 P。
detailEn: McCarthy grouped the levers a marketer controls into four Ps: Product (what need it solves, its features and quality), Price (what it is worth, how it is charged and discounted), Place (where and how it reaches and is delivered to buyers) and Promotion (how advertising, PR, sales promotion and personal selling make buyers aware and keen). The insight is not the list but consistency: all four must point at the same customer and the same position, and one lever working against the others leaks — a premium brand on a bargain shelf loses no matter how loud the ad. Service marketing adds three more Ps: People, Process and Physical Evidence. The classic trap is treating 4P as an inside-out self-expression; modern marketing stresses its mirror, the 4Cs — customer need, cost, convenience and communication: ask what the buyer wants first, then set the four Ps.

oneLiner: 给顾客一个只此一家、且对我有利的具体理由——说不出一句独特的话，广告就只是噪声。
oneLinerEn: Give the buyer one concrete reason that is yours alone and good for them — with no unique line to say, advertising is just noise.
detail: 罗瑟·里夫斯在二十世纪四五十年代提出 USP，一条主张要同时满足三点：向顾客明确说出一个具体好处（买我的牙膏能得到什么）；这个好处必须是竞争对手无法或未曾提出的只此一家；它要强到足以打动大众、驱动购买。经典如 M 豆只溶在口、不溶在手——把产品特性翻成一句独占的利益承诺。USP 与定位理论近亲而不同：USP 从产品本身的独特卖点出发、偏我说什么，定位则从顾客既有心智出发、偏我占哪个位置，很多时候先有心智空位、再去打造或宣称相应 USP。它的难处在于真实且可兑现的独特越来越少——功能趋同的市场里，独特常常要靠品牌、体验或商业模式来承载，一句吹过头的 USP 还会反噬信任。
detailEn: Rosser Reeves set out the USP in the 1940s and 50s: a proposition must meet three tests at once — say one concrete benefit to the buyer (what they get from my toothpaste); make it something rivals cannot or do not claim, ours alone; and make it strong enough to move the mass to buy. The classic line, M&Ms melts in your mouth, not in your hand, turns a product trait into a sole, ownable promise. USP is a near-relative of positioning but not the same: USP starts from the product's own unique selling point and leans toward what I say, while positioning starts from the mind the customer already has and leans toward what slot I take; often the mental gap is found first, then a matching USP is built or claimed. Its difficulty is that genuinely deliverable uniqueness grows scarcer — in a market of converging features the edge must ride on brand, experience or business model, and an over-promised USP can turn against your credibility.

oneLiner: 注意、兴趣、欲望、行动——广告要一步步把路人推到下单，缺一环就断链。
oneLinerEn: Attention, interest, desire, action — advertising must walk a passer-by to purchase step by step; a missing rung breaks the chain.
detail: AIDA 由 19 世纪末的埃·圣埃尔莫·刘易斯概括，是最早的传播效果阶梯：广告先得抓住注意，再唤起兴趣，把兴趣推成占有的欲望，最后促成行动（购买或留资）。它给文案与投放一个朴素指令——开头没有钩子，后面再对也没人看到；所以要标题抓眼、正文养兴趣、证据点火、结尾给一个明确的行动召唤（CTA）。今天把顾客旅程画成漏斗，正源于此：每一环都会有人漏掉，转化率就是一环除以一环。它也招批评——真实决策未必线性、还漏了购后与复购，于是衍生出加信任与行动线索的 AIDCA、以及更贴合社媒的 5A（了解、吸引、问询、行动、拥护）等版本，但 AIDA 仍是看懂一切广告结构的入门语法。
detailEn: Summarised in the late 19th century by E. St. Elmo Lewis, AIDA is the earliest hierarchy of effects in communication: an ad must first seize attention, then arouse interest, turn interest into desire, and finally drive action (a purchase or a lead). It hands copy and media one plain order — with no hook at the top no one ever sees how right the rest is: an eye-catching headline, a body that nurtures interest, proof that ignites desire, and a clear call to action at the end. The modern habit of drawing the customer journey as a funnel comes straight from it — buyers leak at every rung, and the conversion rate is one rung divided by the next. It draws criticism, too: real decisions are rarely linear and it omits post-purchase and repeat buying, hence descendants like AIDCA (adding trust and clues) and the social-media-friendly 5A (aware, appeal, ask, act, advocate). Even so, AIDA remains the entry grammar for reading any ad's structure.

oneLiner: 同一只包，贴牌就能多卖很多——品牌是把认知与信任存进顾客心里、能带来超额回报的无形资产。
oneLinerEn: The same bag sells for far more with the mark on it — a brand is intangible capital of perception and trust that earns an above-normal return.
detail: 品牌资产指因为品牌被知晓、被怎样联想而给产品带来的、超出其功能价值的附加值：同一枚包，贴上某些牌子就能卖出数倍溢价、也更容易被首选——这差额就是资产。大卫·阿克把它拆成品牌知名度、感知质量、品牌联想与品牌忠诚度几项资产（以及相应的负债），凯文·莱恩·凯勒的基于顾客的品牌资产则画出一条从被认出、被记住，到强烈而独特的正面联想，再到共鸣与忠诚的建构阶梯。它的商业意义很实在：品牌是护城河里无形资产的一根支柱，直接支撑定价权与复购，还能被延伸去带动新品线。但它也是最脆弱的资产——一场危机、一次失信就能把多年积累迅速清零，所以品牌既是最值钱的储蓄罐，也是最需要小心照看的账户。
detailEn: Brand equity is the value a product gains beyond its functional worth because of what the brand is known and how it is associated: the same bag commands several times the price and is chosen first when a certain mark is on it — that premium is the asset. David Aaker breaks it into brand awareness, perceived quality, brand associations and brand loyalty (plus their liabilities), while Kevin Lane Keller's customer-based brand equity draws a building ladder from being recognised and recalled, to strong, unique, favourable associations, up to resonance and loyalty. Its business meaning is concrete: the brand is a pillar of the intangible-asset moat, underwriting pricing power and repeat purchase, and can be extended to pull along new lines. Yet it is also the most fragile asset — one crisis, one breach of trust can wipe years of accrual overnight, so a brand is at once the most valuable piggy bank and the account that most needs careful tending.

oneLiner: 广告、公关、促销、社媒、包装……所有触点要讲同一句话——一个声音，一张脸。
oneLinerEn: Advertising, PR, promotion, social, packaging — every touchpoint must say the same thing: one voice, one face.
detail: 唐·舒尔茨等把 IMC 立为一种管理哲学：别让广告、公关、促销、直销、社媒、包装设计各说各话，而从顾客接收端倒推，把所有传播触点整合成一个声音、一张脸，让信息一致、相互放大。它的底层判断是——顾客在无数碎片接触里认识品牌，只要各渠道口径打架，力量就互相抵消；反之，同样的预算因协调一致能产生一加一大于二的叠加。IMC 也随媒介演进而扩展，今天常按付费、自有、赢得三类媒体来统筹：投广告、经营自己的账号与官网、撬动口碑与报道，三者合拍才算整合。难点在于组织内各部门、代理商各管一段、各有 KPI，协调往往败于各自为政，所以它既是传播策略，更是对内部流程与数据的治理。
detailEn: Don Schultz and others raised IMC into a management philosophy: do not let advertising, PR, promotion, direct selling, social and packaging each speak in a different tongue; work backward from the receiver, the customer, integrating every touchpoint into one voice, one face so messages stay consistent and reinforce one another. Its premise is that a customer comes to know a brand across countless fragmentary contacts, so when channels contradict, their forces cancel — while the same budget, coordinated, can yield more than the sum of its parts. IMC has grown with media; today it is often run across the paid, owned and earned triad — buying ads, tending your own accounts and site, and leveraging word of mouth and coverage — which only counts as integrated when the three play in tune. The hard part is organisational: departments and agencies each own a slice and a KPI, and coordination often loses to each to their own — so it is a communications strategy and, just as much, a governance of internal process and data.

oneLiner: 我知道我的广告费有一半是浪费的，问题是我不知道是哪一半——从曝光到转化，广告须能被测量才谈得上优化。
oneLinerEn: Half my advertising is wasted — I just don't know which half. From reach to conversion, advertising must be measurable before it can be optimised.
detail: 常被归到约翰·沃纳梅克名下的那句一半广告费被浪费、却不知是哪一半，正是广告度量的原点难题。可量化的阶梯一层层往上：曝光层看触达与频次、千人成本（CPM）；成本层看按点击或行动计价的 CPC、CPA；响应层看点击率（CTR）与互动；结果层看转化、广告投入产出比（ROAS）与各种归因——把一笔成交的功劳分摊到用户接触过的多个触点。难点在于两类广告天生难测程度不同：效果广告（求即时点击下单）能 A/B、能归因，品牌广告（求长期记忆与偏好）见效慢、易被高估或埋没。因此可信的做法是增量实验：在可比人群中投放与不投放，看真实抬升，而非只信归因模型自报的功劳。它把广告从玄学拉回可验证的投资，与获客成本、单位经济相连——测不准，就无法判断这门生意到底健不健康。
detailEn: The line usually credited to John Wanamaker — half my advertising is wasted, and I don't know which half — is the founding puzzle of advertising measurement. The ladder of measurable layers climbs upward: at exposure, reach, frequency and cost per mille (CPM); at cost, price per click (CPC) and cost per action (CPA); at response, click-through rate (CTR) and engagement; at outcome, conversion, return on ad spend (ROAS) and the many schemes of attribution that split one sale's credit across the touchpoints the user met. The difficulty is that the two kinds of advertising resist measurement unevenly: performance advertising (for an immediate click or order) can be A/B-tested and attributed, while brand advertising (for long-term memory and preference) works slowly and is easily over- or under-counted. The trustworthy move is thus the incrementality test — run the campaign on one comparable audience and not another and watch the true lift, rather than trusting an attribution model's self-reported credit. It pulls advertising from occult craft back toward a verifiable investment, tying to customer-acquisition cost and unit economics: if you cannot measure it, you cannot tell whether the business is actually healthy.

oneLiner: 从发现想要到买后复盘的五步——营销的每一招，都该落在顾客正处的那一步上。
oneLinerEn: Five steps from spotting a want to post-purchase review — every marketing move should land on the step the customer is actually at.
detail: 这是消费者行为学的经典五段：问题识别（现实与期望的落差让想要浮现）到信息搜集（内部记忆加外部广告、口碑、评测）、方案评估（在心里用某些标准比较品牌，往往缩到考虑集里几个候选）、购买决策（临门一脚，还可能被渠道、促销、旁人意见打断）、购后行为（满意或认知失调——买了贵东西后心里打鼓、四处找理由证明自己没做错）。它把顾客为什么买拆成可干预的路径：每一步营销都能下力——唤醒需求、占领信息入口、把自己放进考虑集并给足购买理由、让结账顺畅、用售后与保证消解失调。卷入度决定走哪条路：高价、高风险、买得少是深思熟虑，日常低价常是习惯性、几乎不评估。它与 AIDA 相映——AIDA 是传播者视角，五段是消费者视角；品牌资产则在最后一步替你降低失调。
detailEn: The classic five acts of consumer behaviour: problem recognition (the gap between actual and desired brings a want to the surface), information search (memory plus outside ads, word of mouth, reviews), evaluation of alternatives (weighing a consideration set — the few candidates it narrows to — by some criteria in the mind), purchase decision (the final step, easily interrupted by channel, promotion or a bystander's opinion), and post-purchase behaviour (satisfaction or cognitive dissonance — after a costly buy one frets and hunts for reasons they did not err). It breaks why a customer buys into intervenable paths, so marketing can push at each step: arouse the need, hold the information gate, get into the consideration set with a full reason to buy, make checkout smooth, and dissolve dissonance with after-sales and guarantees. Involvement picks the road: high price, high risk and rare buys are deliberate, while cheap daily goods are habitual, barely evaluated. It mirrors AIDA — AIDA is the communicator's view, the five acts the consumer's — and brand equity steps in at the last act to lower the buyer's dissonance for you.

oneLiner: 导入、成长、成熟、衰退四段曲线——同一产品在不同段落，该打的营销牌完全不同。
oneLinerEn: Introduction, growth, maturity, decline — the right marketing moves differ completely by stage of the same product.
detail: 产品生命周期把品类销售随时间的推移描成一条 S 形加尾巴的四段曲线：导入期销量低、单位成本高、竞手寥寥，钱该花在告知型广告与渠道试用；成长期销量陡升、竞争者涌入，重心转向品牌偏好、扩产能扩渠道，价格开始受压；成熟期增长放缓、市场饱和，价格战与差异化并行，控成本、改市场（新客群新用途）与改产品（新功能新版型）是三把老斧子；衰退期替代品接管，要么收割现金流、要么退出，恋战只会拖垮资源。它提醒管理者：品类曲线与品牌命运不同——碳酸饮料早已成熟，可口可乐却靠全球化与品类扩张续了百年；也要警惕“自我实现”：若因预判衰退而停投，好产品也会被自己判死。另与用户生命周期（AARRR 讲单个用户从获客到留存的五环）互为镜像：一个量产品，一个量顾客。风险在于形状多变：有的品类一步入成熟，有的（时尚品、风口品）从成长直接跳衰退，“生命周期”不是命定时间表，而是一套提醒你在每一段重新审视竞争与现金流的思维框架。
detailEn: The product life cycle traces a category's sales over time as a four-stage curve: in introduction, volumes are low, unit costs high and rivals few, so money buys awareness and trial; in growth, sales climb steeply while competitors pile in, so the job shifts to preference, capacity and distribution as price begins to squeeze; in maturity, growth slows and the market saturates, so price wars and differentiation run side by side, with three classic moves — modify the market (new users, new uses), modify the product (new features, new formats) and modify the mix to hold cost; in decline, substitutes take over and you either harvest the cash flow or exit, because clinging drains resources. It reminds managers that a category's curve is not a brand's fate — carbonated drinks long sat in maturity, yet Coca-Cola bought another century through globalisation and line extension — and that the concept can be self-fulfilling: cut spending on the belief of decline and a fine product dies of the diagnosis. It mirrors the user lifecycle (AARRR's five rings per customer): one measures the product, the other the customer. The caveat is shape: some categories enter maturity in a single swoop; fad goods jump from growth straight into decline. The life cycle is not destiny but a framework forcing you to re-examine competition and cash flow at each stage.

oneLiner: 顾客买的不是产品，是“把某件事办成”——奶昔真正的竞品是香蕉、贝果和“什么都不买”。
oneLinerEn: Customers buy outcomes, not products — the milkshake's real rivals are bananas, bagels and buying nothing at all.
detail: 克里斯坦森著名的奶昔之问：一家快餐连锁想多卖奶昔，问卷反复问“怎样改进产品”，他的团队却换个问法——顾客雇奶昔来干什么活？观察发现近一半卖在早上八点半前，买单人独自开车上班：需要一件能陪路上一个小时、耐吸、不顶饿过头、不脏手、还能给枯燥车程加点乐子的东西——香蕉来得太快、贝果太干、甜甜圈太腻，什么都不买则十点就饿。看清任务后改进反而简单：更稠、加果粒、提早供货、给大杯自助机。理论内核是：产品是工具，需求是功能、情感、社会三层任务的合体；细分市场别按人群画像切，按“情境+任务”切——同一个人早上雇奶昔、晚上给儿子雇玩具。它和颠覆式创新同出一人之手，是另一把刀：多数失败的新品不是不懂用户，而是懂错了任务——满足了问卷里的愿望，没满足通勤路上的小时。
detailEn: Christensen's famous milkshake question: a fast-food chain wanted more milkshakes; surveys kept asking 'how do we improve the product', while his team asked a different one — what job do customers hire the milkshake to do? Nearly half were sold before 8:30 a.m., to solo commuters driving to work: they needed something that would last an hour on the road, stay filling without bloating, keep the hands clean and enliven a dull drive — bananas finished too fast, bagels were dry, donuts cloying, and buying nothing meant hunger by ten. Once the job was seen, improvement became obvious: thicker, fruit chunks, earlier supply, a big-cup self-serve machine. The core idea: products are tools, and demand is a blend of functional, emotional and social jobs; segment not by demographic portraits but by situation plus job — the same person hires a milkshake at dawn and a toy for a son at night. From the same mind as disruptive innovation, it is that theory's other blade: most failed products do not misunderstand users, they misunderstand the job — answering the survey's wish while missing the hour on the commute.

oneLiner: 4P 里唯一直接进账的一条：撇脂、渗透、价值、心理、版本、动态、订阅——七种收钱的姿势，各有各的代价。
oneLinerEn: The only revenue-generating P: skimming, penetration, value, psychological, versioning, dynamic and subscription — each with its own price.
detail: 定价是营销组合里唯一直接产生收入的要素，其余三项都在花钱，而它最常被当作成本问题而非战略问题处理。七种基本姿势：撇脂——先高价收割最不敏感的人群再逐段降价，适合技术领先、仿制慢的产品；渗透——低价快抢份额与网络效应、指望后期变现，适合规模经济显著的生意；价值定价——按买家感知价值而非成本加价定价，前提是能把价值说清并量化；心理定价——利用尾数、锚定（高标低折）与“价格即质量”的信号；版本化——经济舱与商务舱、学生价、家庭装，把不同支付意愿的人分开，是价格歧视的生意名；动态定价——随供需实时改价，机票、网约车、酒店收益管理是主场；订阅——把一次性买卖改成经常性现金流，估值重心随之转向生命周期价值。出招前先查经济学那把尺：价格弹性——需求对价格越不敏感，涨价越安全。两条戒律：降价是最容易发动、最难退出的战争；改价太频会训练顾客“等等再买”，把定价的权威让渡给促销日历。
detailEn: Price is the only element of the marketing mix that generates revenue — the other three spend it — yet it is usually managed as a cost question rather than a strategy. Seven basic stances: skimming — charge high first to harvest the least-sensitive buyers, then step down, fitting technically lead products slow to copy; penetration — buy share and network effects with a low price and monetise later, fitting businesses with strong economies of scale; value pricing — set price from buyer-perceived value rather than cost-plus, provided the value can be articulated and measured; psychological pricing — odd endings, anchoring through high list and discount, and price-as-quality signals; versioning — economy and business class, student rates, family packs — separating willingness to pay, the commercial name of price discrimination; dynamic pricing — repricing with live supply and demand, home turf of airlines, ride-hailing and hotel revenue management; subscription — turning one-off sales into recurring cash flow, moving valuation weight onto lifetime value. Before choosing, consult the economist's ruler: price elasticity — the less sensitive demand, the safer a rise. Two rules to keep: a price cut is the easiest war to start and the hardest to exit; and repricing too often trains customers to 'wait for the sale', handing pricing authority to the promotion calendar.

oneLiner: 一次曝光的买卖在百毫秒内完成竞价——实时竞价、需求方与供给方平台组成的自动市场，效率高，水也深。
oneLinerEn: A single impression trades in a hundred-millisecond auction — RTB with demand- and supply-side platforms: efficient markets, murky ones too.
detail: 程序化广告把“买广告位”从人和人谈价变成机器和机器竞价：媒体每亮出一次曝光机会，交易系统就向各需求方平台（DSP）广播询问，平台依据这个受众的数据——是否目标人群、值多少钱——实时出价，最高者得，全程约百毫秒，此谓实时竞价（RTB）；卖方通过供给方平台（SSP）把流量打包上架，数据管理平台（DMP）提供人群标签。优点是精准、可规模化、按人投放而非按版位投放，长尾流量也变得可买；但它同时把沃纳梅克之问升级到技术层：交易链条层层抽成且不透明，虚假流量、机器人点击与品牌安全（广告出现在恶劣内容旁）是慢性病，“买到的曝光”与“真被看见的曝光”又隔一层。第二大浪是隐私收紧：第三方 cookies 逐步退场、移动端要求用户授权，定向能力被砍，第一方数据（自有顾客与情境数据）回潮，大平台自建闭环。应对与度量同根：用增量实验证明有效、用可见性标准证明被看、把预算当投资而非成本来核算。
detailEn: Programmatic advertising turns buying ad space from negotiation between people into auction between machines: whenever a publisher offers an impression, an exchange broadcasts the question to demand-side platforms (DSPs), which bid in real time based on data about that viewer — whether they match the target and what they are worth — and the highest wins in roughly a hundred milliseconds; that is real-time bidding (RTB). Sellers pool inventory through supply-side platforms (SSPs), while data platforms supply audience segments. The gains are precision, scale, buying people instead of slots, and a monetisable long tail; but it also upgrades Wanamaker's problem to the technical layer: opaque layers of take-rate, phantom traffic, bot clicks and brand safety (your ad beside awful content) are chronic ills, and 'an impression bought' sits one layer from 'an impression seen'. The second wave is privacy: third-party cookies fading, mobile requiring explicit consent, targeting cut back, first-party data returning to favour, and large platforms building walled gardens. The response shares roots with measurement: prove effect with incrementality experiments, prove viewing with visibility standards, and account for budget as investment, not cost.

oneLiner: 广告是付钱买版面，公关是赢得第三方自愿转述——可信度更高，也最经不起撒谎。
oneLinerEn: Advertising buys space; public relations wins unpaid retelling — more credible, and the least able to survive a lie.
detail: 在付费、自有、赢得三类媒体中，公关经营最难买的“赢得”：报道、口碑、推荐与品牌词搜索。第三方背书自带可信度加成，但你控制不了它说什么、说多大——这决定了公关的产品是新闻价值：故事是否有时效、有数据、有面孔、切中公共议题，而不是自我表扬的通稿。危机公关是压力测试：社媒时代回应窗口从旧训“黄金四小时”缩到按分钟计；实践排序常被做反——先法律口径、后人情，公众先读到的是冷漠。可用框架四个字：快（第一时间表态）、真（承认已知事实、共情受害者，道歉不等于定责）、一（单一口径发声，免得部门版本打架）、改（整改可见可查）。日常一侧，口碑可用品牌搜索量、净情绪与转介率监测——推荐正是 AARRR 的第四个 R，社会认同的心理机制见“影响力原则”条。最深一层：声誉是复利资产，平日好感是危机时的减震器；把公关当成本中心削减，等于退掉消防队的保险费。
detailEn: Among paid, owned and earned media, public relations runs the hardest to buy — the earned: coverage, word of mouth, referrals, branded search. Third-party endorsement carries built-in credibility, but you control neither what it says or how loudly — which makes newsworthy story the PR product: timeliness, data, a human face, a live public issue, not a self-congratulatory release. Crisis communication is the stress test: in the social era the response window has shrunk from the old 'golden four hours' to minutes; priorities are often inverted — legal wording first, humanity second, so the public reads coldness first. A usable frame in four words: fast (speak first), true (concede known facts, empathise with victims — apology is not admission of liability), one (a single voice, not warring departments), fix (remediation visible and verifiable). On ordinary days, word of mouth is tracked via branded search volume, net sentiment and referral rates — referral being AARRR's fourth R, with social proof's psychology covered under the principles of influence. The deepest layer: reputation compounds, and goodwill banked is the crisis shock absorber; cutting PR as a cost centre is cancelling the fire brigade to save on premiums.

oneLiner: 满意只是不被投诉的及格线，推荐与复购才是忠诚的分数——一道题简化了世界，也埋了坑。
oneLinerEn: Satisfaction is merely the no-complaint pass mark; recommending and rebuying measure loyalty — one question simplified the world and buried traps.
detail: 满意度研究的理论地基是“期望不一致”：满意不是体验的绝对值，而是体验与期望之差——广告把期望吹高，好产品也会让人失望。但满意与购买之间有一条裂缝：赖赫尔德的经典发现是“非常满意”的顾客照样流失——满意只是门槛，忠诚才是行为：复购、推荐、对竞争者的报价不再敏感。NPS 把忠诚折成一道题：“你有多大可能把它推荐给朋友？”九十分以上为推荐者、六十分以下为贬损者，两者占比之差即得分；它因简单、可跨期跨业比较而流行，也因过度简化而遭反噬：不同文化打分尺度不同（中庸文化天然压低分数）、单一题目对改进缺乏操作性（员工知道分数却不知为何）、激励扭曲的诱惑尤其防不住——只向满意客户发问、用奖励换高分，让指标空心化，赖赫尔德本人晚年也批评 NPS 被用成“又一个应付的分数”。严肃的做法：把 NPS 与流失率、复购、留存曲线并排看，把追访“为什么”固定成流程——它最终连着单位经济学里生命周期价值的分母：留存率。
detailEn: The theoretical ground of satisfaction research is expectation-disconfirmation: satisfaction is not the absolute of experience but its gap to expectation — hype the expectation and a good product still disappoints. Yet a crack runs between satisfaction and purchase: Reichheld's classic finding was that 'very satisfied' customers switch anyway — satisfaction is a threshold; loyalty is behaviour: rebuying, recommending, insensitivity to rivals' quotes. NPS folds loyalty into one question: 'How likely are you to recommend this to a friend?' Scores of nine or ten count as promoters, six or below as detractors, and the gap between their shares is the score. It spread because it is simple and comparable across time and industry, and drew fire for oversimplification: response scales differ across cultures (middle-way cultures depress scores), a single question lacks operability (staff know the number, not the why), and incentive distortion tempts all — surveying only satisfied customers, buying high scores with rewards, hollowing the metric; Reichheld himself later lamented NPS reduced to 'yet another score to manage'. The serious practice: read NPS beside churn, repeat purchase and retention curves, and make the follow-up question 'why' a standing process — it ends at the denominator of lifetime value in unit economics: retention.
